place_name: Troll Hole (Gray Slab), Pass Creek Canyon, Lost River Range, Idaho
approach_stated: Climbing is never more than 100 m from Pass Creek; a gravel road runs through the canyon; wall is up-canyon from Campsite Wall beside a large cave
summit_or_glacier: no - single-pitch limestone slab, road-accessible canyon

evidence.fact: Clean limestone slab beside a large cave, up the canyon from Campsite Wall; three routes, two bolted; MP lists them Sport.
Pass Creek Canyon: a well-maintained gravel road bisects the range; climbing is never more than one hundred meters from Pass Creek.

note: Roadside limestone canyon crag.

place_name: Harkness Canyon, Portneuf Range, near McCammon, Idaho
approach_stated: Hike takes about 1.5-2 hours without an ATV (about 2 miles up a ridgeline trail then off-trail); area description says long approach (1 to 2 hours)
summit_or_glacier: no summit or glacier; limestone band 30-250 ft

evidence.fact: Limestone band 30-250 ft; it has a long approach (1 to 2 hours); remote, alpine feel.
Getting There: hike up the ridgeline about 2 miles; the hike takes about 1.5-2 hours without an ATV.

note: Single-pitch sport climbing but the stated approach exceeds 60 min, so alpine under the owner's rule.

place_name: South Dome, Lion Creek Drainage, Selkirk Crest, North Idaho
approach_stated: From the parking at the end of Lion Creek Road: trail 150 yards, cross creek, cairned talus/scree hike to base of slab; no time stated
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; long friction slab routes (Lion King 1300 ft, 15 pitches, rappel descent); not a summit finish

evidence.fact: Type: Sport, Alpine, 1300 ft, 15 pitches. From parking at end of Lion Creek Road follow trail 150 yards, cross creek, talus to slab.
Large dome visible from the road to the parking; cairned paths to creek crossing, then boulder and scree hike to the slabs.

note: Approach described is short (road-end parking, 150 yd trail + talus) but no time is stated; MP tags Lion King Sport+Alpine (long multi-pitch). Leans crag on approach.

place_name: The Main Face, Mt Kineo, Moosehead Lake, Maine
approach_stated: Best approach is by boat/canoe across Moosehead Lake to the base, or trail from the golf course; long drive and/or paddle; no time stated
summit_or_glacier: 800 ft face tops out on Mt Kineo; descent is a bushwhack (island trails end half a mile from top-out)

evidence.fact: Face juts 800 ft from Moosehead Lake; secluded due to the long drive and/or paddle; best approach by boat.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 800 ft, 7 pitches, Grade IV; full-day outing; trails end half a mile from top-out, descent hellish.

note: Not road-accessible (boat approach), Grade IV, top-out with bushwhack descent; MP tags Trad+Alpine.

place_name: The Castle, Chimney Canyon, Sandia Mountains, New Mexico
approach_stated: Approach time ~35 minutes from the car (down the Muralla Grande trail, then down a rocky ridge to the Tecolote/Castle saddle)
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; a detached fin/rib, descent via El Tecolote/Castle gully

evidence.fact: Approach time to here is ~35 minutes from the car; the Castle is the obvious detached fin forming the right side of the gully.

note: Approach is downhill from the crest; the uphill return time is not stated.

place_name: The Pulpit, Upper La Cueva Canyon, Sandia Mountains, New Mexico
approach_stated: Via La Luz trail from above (Sandia Crest) or below; no time stated; page says any ascent guarantees a long day
summit_or_glacier: summit finish: a true spire requiring a rappel descent from the summit

evidence.fact: Due to its distance from the Sandia Crest, sees little action and any ascent guarantees a long day; a true spire with rappel descent.

note: Alpine on summit finish; approach time itself not stated.

place_name: Hinkey Summit, Santa Rosa Range (Paradise Valley), Nevada
approach_stated: The approach to the base of the climbing wall is extremely easy and takes just a few minutes (parking at Hinkey Summit, 14.5 mi up NF-084)
summit_or_glacier: no; multi-pitch routes may top out on the formation, walk-off descent east

evidence.fact: The approach to the base of the climbing wall is extremely easy and takes just a few minutes.
Follow Hinkey Summit Road about 14.5 miles to Hinkey Summit; MP lists Don't Call Me White and Solid Silver as Sport.

note: "Route to Nowhere" is not listed on the MP area page (unknown-FA route mentioned in comments); type unknown.

place_name: Boulder Island, Leigh Lake, Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming
approach_stated: From Leigh Lake parking, trail ~3/4 mile toward Leigh Lake then signs to the portage; island is reached by swim or paddle
summit_or_glacier: no; toprope boulder/island, anchors reached by scrambling the east side

evidence.fact: A lazy afternoon: swim or paddle to the island for scenic toproping off bolts on the west and northwest sides.
From Leigh Lake parking follow the trail north; after approximately 3/4 of a mile follow signs toward the portage.

note: Short trail + swim; no summit or glacier. MP types TR (tagged Alpine on route pages).

place_name: Lost Temple Spire, Deep Lake Area, Wind River Range, Wyoming
approach_stated: Approach as for the Cirque of the Towers, then up to Clear Lake and Deep Lake (backpacking approach; camping at Clear/Deep Lake); no time stated
summit_or_glacier: summit finish on a detached spire off East Temple Peak; roadless backcountry

evidence.fact: A lost spire off the eastern prow of East Temple Peak; walk up to the lake below, multiple pitches of granite.
Approach as for the Cirque, heading up toward Clear Lake then Deep Lake; camping at Clear Lake or above-treeline Deep Lake.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 7 pitches.

note: Wind River backcountry spire; clearly alpine.

place_name: Superior Apron (south apron of Mt Superior), Little Cottonwood Canyon, Utah
approach_stated: Approach is 20-40 minutes to the routes, from a pullout on Hwy 210 just past Snowbird Entry 4, up scrub oak and the talus apron
summit_or_glacier: no; 5th-class slab routes on the apron below the peak (the South Ridge alpine route is a separate line at the western edge)

evidence.fact: Rock climbs accessed from the apron of Mt Superior; approach is 20-40 minutes to the routes.
Type: Trad, 150 ft, 2 pitches, Grade II; alternate finish to Suicide Slab's 4th/5th pitches.

note: MP files these under Superior Apron (Little Cottonwood Canyon), not the Mt Superior/Monte Cristo alpine area our area_id names; the area may be misfiled.

place_name: Penstemon Dome (East Face), Courtright Reservoir, Southern Sierra, California
approach_stated: East face: approach takes 30-45 minutes (standard approach from Maxon parking then around to the back); dome as a whole: access takes about 20 to 30 minutes
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; dome face routes

evidence.fact: Standard approach from the parking area then wander around to the back side; the approach takes 30-45 minutes.
From the Maxon parking lot down the 4WD trail and creek; access to the dome takes about 20 to 30 minutes.

note: Road-accessible reservoir dome; MP lists all three sample routes Sport.

place_name: Southern Cross, May Lake Area, Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite NP, California
approach_stated: About 3 miles and 1000 ft elevation gain from the May Lake trailhead (rising traverse from May Lake or undocumented trail then straight up); no time stated
summit_or_glacier: no summit or glacier stated; 500 ft, 3-pitch Grade II buttress routes

evidence.fact: Buttress NNE of May Lake; about 3 miles and 1000' elevation gain from the May Lake trailhead.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 500 ft, 3 pitches, Grade II; climbing described as more alpine than Tuolumne domes.

note: Verdict rests on the stated 3 mi / 1000 ft approach (no time stated); a 3-mile approach is over an hour at normal pace. Same MP area also holds the ca_that_scary_looking_buttress routes.

place_name: Southern Cross (same buttress), May Lake Area, Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite NP, California
approach_stated: About 3 miles and 1000 ft elevation gain from the May Lake trailhead; no time stated
summit_or_glacier: no summit or glacier stated; 500 ft, 3-pitch Grade II routes

evidence.fact: Lists Fear of Fun AKA Southern Comfort, The Astraphobia Treatment AKA Southern Belle, Wet My Pants AKA Southern Fried, all Trad.
About 3 miles and 1000' elevation gain from the May Lake trailhead.

note: MP holds these three routes in the Southern Cross area, same as ca_southern_cross: likely a duplicate area to merge. Verdict from stated 3 mi / 1000 ft distance, no time stated.

place_name: Cracks At The Dam Wall, Courtright Reservoir, Southern Sierra, California
approach_stated: The wall is off the road at the dam area (drive to the dam)
summit_or_glacier: no; 45 ft single-pitch cracks

evidence.fact: Little wall with fun cracks at the dam area; drive to the dam, the wall is off the road.
Type: Trad, TR, 45 ft.

note: Roadside. Gentle, Jeff, Schroeder are listed Trad+TR on MP.

place_name: Sideshow (Lower), Lake George, Mammoth Lakes Area, Eastern Sierra, California
approach_stated: From parking, west path around Lake George 0.4 mile to a stream, climbers trail up 200 yards, cross Crystal Lake outlet, talus to the wall; no time stated
summit_or_glacier: no; 60-80 ft single-pitch bolted wall

evidence.fact: Short 60-80 ft routes, generous bolting; follow the west path around Lake George 0.4 mile, climbers trail 200 yards, then talus.
Lower wall easily reached by climbing the talus; lists Inspection Rejection, Mariposa Lily, Polar Bear Princess as Sport.

note: Stated distance is well under a mile plus talus; no time given. MP route pages tag Sport+Alpine.

place_name: Locke Rock, near Maxson Meadow, Courtright Reservoir, Southern Sierra, California
approach_stated: Allow two hours to hike from the Cliff Lakes parking lot (past Leopold Dome and Maxson Meadow)
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; large granite dome, 880-1120 ft, 5-7 pitch routes

evidence.fact: Park at the Cliff Lakes lot, trail past Leopold Dome and Maxson Meadow; allow two hours to hike from the parking lot.
Type: Trad, 900 ft, 5 pitches.

note: Stated 2-hour approach makes it alpine under the rule.

place_name: Swiss Cheese Wall, Courtright Reservoir, Southern Sierra, California
approach_stated: From the Power Dome parking, hike the back side of Power Dome to Penstemon creek, cross, head uphill to the top of the wall on a rock-marked climbers trail; no time or distance stated
summit_or_glacier: no; 3-pitch wall routes (400-450 ft, Grade II)

evidence.fact: From Power Dome parking hike the backside of Power Dome to Penstemon creek, cross, uphill to top of the wall.
Type: Trad, 450 ft, 3 pitches, Grade II.

note: No approach time stated; nearby Penstemon Dome east face is stated 30-45 min, suggesting crag, but not stated for this wall. Slasher Dome, which MP says lies further down the canyon from Swiss Cheese Wall off the same Power Dome parking, is stated 45 minutes.

place_name: 64th Birthday Area (SE face of Punk Rock), Courtright Reservoir, Southern Sierra, California
approach_stated: Punk Rock is beside the Maxon parking lot; closest climbs about 5 minutes from the car; this area is reached by a climbers trail and a talus traverse from the wilderness trailhead sign
summit_or_glacier: no; 120-180 ft single-pitch slab routes

evidence.fact: From the Maxon parking lot the dome is on your right; the closest climbs are about 5 minutes from the car.
Far left of the East Face of Punk Rock; climbers trail from wilderness trailhead sign, traverse across talus to the base.

note: Roadside dome.

place_name: Slasher Dome, south of Power Dome, Courtright Reservoir, Southern Sierra, California
approach_stated: Allow 45 minutes for the approach from the Power Dome parking area
summit_or_glacier: no; 90 ft dome, single-pitch routes on the southwest face

evidence.fact: Slasher Dome: ninety foot dome south of Power Dome, further down canyon than Swiss Cheese Wall; allow 45 minutes for the approach.

note: Route types from MP search listing: The Slasher Sport, Slash and Burn Trad, The Ripper Trad.

place_name: Starlight Peak (14,198 ft), Palisades, High Sierra, California
approach_stated: Not stated on the area page; accessed from North Palisade routes
summit_or_glacier: summit: a fourteener next to North Palisade; summit block is a 30 ft obelisk (5.9 moves); Palisades setting

evidence.fact: 14,198 ft fourteener near North Palisade; true summit is a pointy obelisk-like 30 ft boulder, accessed quickly from North Pal.

note: Sample routes (The X, West Pillar, West Rib) are not listed on MP's Starlight Peak page, so the place identity is inferred from the area name only; types unknown. If this is the Palisades peak it is clearly alpine.

place_name: Leggat Spire, Branham Lakes, Tobacco Root Mountains, Montana
approach_stated: Fairly easy and short approach through sparse timber on the far side of Branham Lakes, west for around a mile (from Branham Campground)
summit_or_glacier: southeast spur of Leggat Mountain; multi-pitch (4-6 pitches, 550-850 ft) north/northeast faces; finish not stated; described as fairly remote

evidence.fact: Leggat Spire, SE spur of Leggat Mountain; fairly remote though approach rather short by Montana backcountry standards; ~1 mile from Branham Lakes.
MP search lists Legacy: Trad, Alpine, 6 pitches, 850 ft; Legatee: Trad, Alpine, 4 pitches, 550 ft.

note: Approach ~1 mile (likely under an hour) but it is a mountain spur with Grade II alpine multi-pitch; summit finish not stated.

place_name: The Cooler, Ainger Lake / Frazier Lake basin, Bridger Range, Montana
approach_stated: From the meadow parking, climb the hill north, descend into the cirque and work east along Frazier Lake, then down-right to the block; no time or distance stated
summit_or_glacier: no; 70 ft limestone block, single pitch

evidence.fact: Limestone block; reached over a hill into the cirque and along Frazier Lake; noted as a stop on two-day trips to Vanishing Point.
Approach switchbacks up the hillside to a crest then drops into the Frazier Lake or Ainger Lake basin; no time given.

note: Single-pitch sport (MP tags Sport, Alpine, Grade II) in a cirque over a ridge; approach length not stated.

place_name: Britney Spears Arete (beside Phat One Buttress), Emigrant Gulch, Paradise Valley, Montana
approach_stated: Visible from the road; hike up the 4x4 road, scree trail, gully and a fixed hose to the base; no time or distance stated
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; 300 ft, 3-pitch arete

evidence.fact: Britney Spears Arete is very obvious to see from the road; approach up 4x4 road, scree, gully and a fixed rubber hose.
MP search lists Oops, I Did It Again: Sport, Alpine, 3 pitches, 300 ft; Unknown: Trad, TR, Alpine, 100 ft.

note: Approach looks short (visible from road) but no time is stated.

place_name: The Bone Saw (east face of Hardscrabble Peak), Fairy Lake, Bridger Range, Montana
approach_stated: Overall the approach takes between an hour and an hour and a half (from parking past Fairy Lake trailhead, up a meadow, off-trail through a gap and scree)
summit_or_glacier: ridge/summit finish: from the last belay follow the easy ridge to the summit of Hardscrabble Peak, walk off

evidence.fact: Feature leading up the east face of Hardscrabble Peak; the approach takes between an hour and an hour and a half.
Descent: from the last belay follow the obvious easy ridge to the summit of Hardscrabble, then walk down.

note: Both approach (>60 min) and summit finish make it alpine. MP area page lists EZ Direct and Original Route as Trad (EZ Direct route page: Trad, Alpine, 650 ft, 4 pitches, Grade II).

place_name: St. Paul Peak (east face), Cabinet Mountains Wilderness, Montana
approach_stated: Approach from St. Paul Lake or Cliff Lake (wilderness lakes; camping advised in established sites); no time stated
summit_or_glacier: 1,200 ft east face of a wilderness peak; routes 8-10 pitches, Trad/Alpine

evidence.fact: East face is high-quality (for alpine) quartzite, 1,200 ft; approach from St. Paul Lake or Cliff Lake; camp in established sites.
MP search lists Paradise Lost Trad, Alpine, 8 pitches, 1200 ft; Northeast Arete Trad, Alpine, 10 pitches, 1300 ft.

note: Roadless wilderness peak face with lake approach and camping; alpine.

place_name: The Rain Cave, Wolverine Bowl, Bridger Range, Montana
approach_stated: From the parking lot it is a 1 hour hike to Wolverine (45 min if hiking quickly), then a short climbers trail past the Lower Replica and up a scree trail to the cave
summit_or_glacier: no; single-pitch sport routes in a small cave/grotto

evidence.fact: From the parking lot it is a 1 hour hike to Wolverine (45min if hiking quickly).
From the meadow follow the climbers trail past the Lower Replica, then a faint scree trail up to the small cave; Phantom and Henry's Route are Sport.

note: Borderline: stated 45-60 min to the bowl plus a short extra uphill to the cave; single-pitch sport, no summit.

place_name: Pollock Mountain Spur, above Logan Pass, Glacier National Park, Montana
approach_stated: Park at the Logan Pass lot; the Spur face is visible from the visitor center; ascend the scree field to the base of the cliff; no time or distance stated
summit_or_glacier: Grade III, 5-7 pitch Trad/Alpine routes on a spur of Pollock Mountain; finish not stated (the mountain's summit is reached by a separate standard route from Lunch Creek)

evidence.fact: Trad, Alpine, 800 ft, 5 pitches, Grade III; directly north of Logan Pass, face visible from visitors center lot; scree to base.
Park in the Logan Pass parking lot for the Pollock Mountain Spur climbs; summit standard route starts at Lunch Creek.

note: Approach looks short (scree from a visible road-pass lot) but no time is stated; Grade III mountain-face setting leans alpine.

place_name: Right Flank, Eagle Cliff, Franconia Notch, New Hampshire
approach_stated: About a 50 minute uphill hike (Greenleaf Trail about 40 minutes, then a cairned climbers trail)
summit_or_glacier: no; single long pitches (70 m rope to lower) off a grassy ledge

evidence.fact: Getting There: about a 50 minute uphill hike; follow the Green Leaf Trail for about 40 minutes, then climbers trail.
Routes start off a grassy ledge; long pitches, most need a 70M rope to lower off; lists both routes Trad.

note: MP route page tags Wet Shoes Sound Mind Trad, Alpine (110 ft), but approach is stated under an hour and routes are lowered off.

place_name: Broken Blade Ridge, Pinnacle Valley, Sandia Mountains, New Mexico
approach_stated: Reach the base of Tombstone then traverse southwest across the valley; no time stated
summit_or_glacier: ridge/summit finish: 1000 ft, 4-pitch Grade II ridge climb that ends at the summit, walk off east

evidence.fact: Trad, Alpine, 1000 ft, 4 pitches, Grade II; last pitch a hand crack to the summit; walk off east.
Ridge on the south side of Pinnacle Valley; reach the base of Tombstone then traverse southwest; lists The Scabbard Trad.

note: Alpine on ridge-to-summit finish; approach time not stated.

place_name: Mineral Wall, The Wild Granites, Toiyabe Range (near Kingston), Nevada
approach_stated: Cross over the col below the Pyramid and aim for the large buttress across the gully (from parking at the base of the mountain via dirt roads); no time or distance stated
summit_or_glacier: no glacier; golden buttress left of the main dome; remote desert granite

evidence.fact: Golden buttress left of the main dome; cross over the col below the Pyramid, aim for the buttress across the gully.
Big granite walls in the remoteness of the Nevada desert, off the south flank of Toiyabe Range Peak; dirt-road access, park at the mountain base.

note: Approach crosses a col, length unstated; remote setting. MP lists Drama Daze and Gold Dust as Trad.
